experiments.purpose: Empirical validation that `consuming` overloads on `where Left: ~Copyable, Right: ~Copyable` extensions subsume the implicit-Copyable non-consuming functor surface (map / flatMap / fold / swapped) without consumer-site regression.
experiments.statusDetail: Single set of `consuming` variants on `where Left: ~Copyable, Right: ~Copyable` shipped as the canonical functor surface in `Sources/Either Primitives/` (Either+Map.swift / Either+FlatMap.swift / Either+Fold.swift / Either+Swap.swift). Equal-arm `map { f }` / `flatMap { f }` are also `consuming`. For Copyable arms, Swift's ownership system implicitly inserts copies — no separate non-consuming overload is required.
experiments.supersededBy: Consuming-only functor surface shipped in swift-either-primitives main target

experiments.purpose: Empirically verify which Either functor methods admit ~Escapable arms. CONFIRMED: swapped (both arms), value(of:), map(right:) / map(left:) on un-transformed arm. BLOCKED with diagnostics: map(left:right:), flatMap, fold for full ~Escapable arms (Gap A — closure-parameter lifetime dependencies).
experiments.statusDetail: All CONFIRMED variants compile clean across triple toolchain. BLOCKED variants documented in source comments with verbatim diagnostics. Outputs/build.txt + Outputs/build-6.4-dev.txt capture build logs.
